questions.0.explain.t: SAST is static analysis: it reads the code and looks for insecure patterns without running the application.

questions.0.options.0.t: The running application, sending HTTP requests the way an attacker would

questions.0.options.1.t: The source code (or bytecode) without executing it

questions.0.options.2.t: Third-party dependencies and the known CVEs of each version

questions.0.options.3.t: The network traffic between the application's services in production

questions.1.explain.t: Without executing the code, SAST can flag unreachable paths and cannot see the behavior of the real environment.

questions.1.options.0.t: It only works after the deploy, when the application is already running

questions.1.options.1.t: It produces false positives and does not see runtime configuration problems

questions.1.options.2.t: It cannot analyze code written in Python or JavaScript

questions.1.options.3.t: It needs access to the production environment to read the configuration

questions.1.q.t: What is a typical limitation of SAST?

questions.2.explain.t: Calibrating rules and gates by severity keeps developers' trust without hiding risk.

questions.2.options.0.t: Turning off the rules that raise the most alerts so the team does not get tired

questions.2.options.1.t: Tune rules to the project, block only high severity and treat the rest as backlog

questions.2.options.2.t: Running the analysis only once a quarter, before the audit

questions.2.options.3.t: Ignoring the result and relying only on DAST to find the problems

questions.2.q.t: What is the best way to reduce SAST noise without losing coverage?
